column1: # Supplementary Table 3. The 80 studies of the analysis (67 with the authors' list and 13 with our own derived list, which include Ketchesin 2023, Frohlich 2024 and Pai 2019), with the availability of the authors' hit list, sample meta-data and expression matrix.
# Availability was checked against public records during October 2026.

# Availability calls: in article = in the article's main text or a supplementary file of the article (journal access may be needed); public external = in a public repository or data portal outside the article; by request = stated to be available on request or behind a registration; controlled = access-controlled repository (application required); not available = the source states it is not released, or only a non-qualifying form exists (group means only, a dead address, a subset); not found = searched for and not found, with no statement either way; unknown = not determined. For sample meta-data, an in article or public external call requires per-sample diagnosis plus at least one of age, sex, pH or PMI.

# Sample-metadata codes (sample_metadata_codes): D diagnosis, G age, S sex, H pH, P postmortem interval (PMI), R RIN or other RNA quality measure (including 18S/28S and 3'/5' ratios), A agonal state or agonal score, + any other per-sample variable (named in sample_metadata_other_variables). Upper case = recorded per sample (or per matched pair) in the source named; lower case = given only as a group-level value in that source. Letters follow the order D G S H P R A +. A blank code means the per-sample variables are not itemized in this table.

# Columns: study (first author and year); pmid; year; cohort_cluster_or_status (cohort cluster of the study as defined in the paper: cmc+mssm+pitt+libd, stanley, aus, harvard, pritzker; independent = the study forms its own cluster; several clusters separated by semicolons = the study pools donors from several banks and belongs to the cluster of each (brain_other:PMID = a bank outside the named clusters, one study)); for each of hit_list, sample_metadata and expression_matrix, a *_call (availability call) and a *_where (where a reader can get it: accession, URL, or supplement file and table number); sample_metadata_codes; sample_metadata_other_variables (names of the + variables, and of group-level variables for rows coded in lower case).

# Abbreviations: SZ schizophrenia; BD or BPD bipolar disorder; MDD major depressive disorder; DE differentially expressed; DLPFC dorsolateral prefrontal cortex; PMI postmortem interval; RIN RNA integrity number; GEO Gene Expression Omnibus; SRA Sequence Read Archive; ENA European Nucleotide Archive; EGA European Genome-phenome Archive; dbGaP database of Genotypes and Phenotypes; SMRI Stanley Medical Research Institute (its Neuropathology Consortium and Array Collection data are in the SNCID database, sncid.stanleyresearch.org); LIBD Lieber Institute for Brain Development; LCM laser-capture microdissection; CMC CommonMind Consortium; NeMO Neuroscience Multi-omic Data Archive.
# code: <repository link to be added on release>

# Columns reanalysed_from_expression, reanalysis_route, datasets_reanalysed, samples_reanalysed, subjects_reanalysed_cases, subjects_reanalysed_controls: every study contributes the authors' hit list; Yes = in addition I re-fitted schizophrenia against control from the study's own sample-level expression data; Partly = only part of the study's data (a validation cohort) were available; No = the study is represented by the authors' hit list only (no re-analysis). A dataset is one brain region or one sorted, laser-captured or cell-class population of a series. Samples are arrays or libraries; subjects are persons, counted once even when profiled in several regions of the same series (cases and controls separately). Samples are blank for PsychAD and the single-nucleus pH test, which were analysed as donor-by-cell-class pseudobulks.

# list_source: authors = the authors' hit list is used; derived = our own list from public expression data by one fixed rule (limma ~ diagnosis + age + sex, Benjamini-Hochberg within dataset, FDR < 0.05), used because the authors' list is not usable (not published or targeted). hit_list_call = derived for these rows; the authors' own list is described after 'The authors' list'.
# Re-analysis columns are blank for the 13 studies with our own derived list (list_source = derived): their list is itself our analysis of the public expression data.
